title: 3.5.12 Lab: Build a Small Nested-Object Structure
description: Build an object with a nested object and an array of objects, then read values out of it. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Outer object
steps.instructions: Create a variable named order and assign it an object literal.

steps.title: Nested object
steps.instructions: Give the order a customer property whose value is another object with at least a name field.

steps.title: Array of objects
steps.instructions: Give the order an items property whose value is an array of at least two objects, each with a name and a price.

steps.title: Read the nested object
steps.instructions: Print the customer's name using a chain: the order, a dot, customer, a dot, name.

steps.title: Walk the array and read each field
steps.instructions: Loop over the items array and print each item's name and price using bracket index then dot field.

requirements.title: nested object built
requirements.description: An object literal holds another object literal. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)

requirements.title: array of objects built
requirements.description: An array literal holds at least one object literal. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)

requirements.title: nested chain read
requirements.description: Reads a.b.c with at least two dots. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)

requirements.title: index then field read
requirements.description: Reads arr[i].field. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)

requirements.title: loop present
requirements.description: Contains a for loop. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))

requirements.title: order holds a customer object and a list of items, and each item is printed
requirements.description: order.customer has a name, order.items is an array of at least two objects each with a name and a price, and the customer and every item are printed. Help: 3.5.9 (Nested Objects)
requirements.hint: Build order with a customer object (with a name) and an items array holding at least two objects, each with a name and a price. Then print the customer name and loop over the items.

checks.expr: order && order.customer && typeof order.customer.name === 'string' && Array.isArray(order.items) && order.items.length >= 2 && order.items.every(i => i && typeof i.name === 'string' && typeof i.price === 'number') && output.length >= 1 + order.items.length
checks.fail: order needs a customer object with a name and an items array of at least two objects, each with a name (text) and a price (number). Print the customer name, then one line for every item.
